entry.evidence: However, the existing diagrams lack adequate information on the third main ecological steering factor: nutrients.

steps.action: The authors state the gap: classical multi-ion diagrams (Stiff, Piper, Maucha) were built for hydrogeology and lack nutrient information needed for ecohydrology and policy.
steps.quote: However, the existing diagrams lack adequate information on the third main ecological steering factor: nutrients.

steps.action: They review earlier ecohydrological diagrams (Van Wirdum's Ionic Ratio, Wassen et al.'s adapted Stiff) and report finding none that covers all four main nutrients.
steps.quote: we found no water quality diagrams that encompass all the main eco(hydro)logically relevant nutrients NO3, NH4, PO4, and K

steps.action: They postulate that ecohydrologically relevant diagrams would help researchers and managers, and restrict the scope to fresh water (Cl < 300 mg/l).
steps.quote: We postulate that more ecohydrologically relevant water quality diagrams may aid the work of academic ecohydrologists and water and nature managers.

steps.action: They select 10 parameters (NO3, NH4, PO4, K, Cl, Ca, Fe, SO4, Na, HCO3) by ecological and hydrological information value and common availability; Na and HCO3 are added for visual comparability (Table 1).
steps.quote: The selection of parameters for an ecohydrologically relevant water quality diagram was based on its envisaged ability to provide information

steps.action: They had planned a single adapted diagram, then revised the plan to several diagram forms using the same parameters, because user preferences differed.
steps.quote: During our research it appeared personal preferences on diagram types may differ, so we decided to present a number of different diagrams

steps.action: They define the ion pairings (Na-Cl, Ca-HCO3, Fe-SO4, NH4-NO3, K-PO4) and two Maucha-based forms (via Broch & Yake) plus two Stiff-based forms (Stiff-A, Stiff-B), with K separated from Na.
steps.quote: We defined two adapted diagrams based on the Maucha diagram and two on the Stiff diagram.

steps.action: After trials showed that the inward-pointing arrows of the Jester diagram distorted minor-ion concentrations, they redesigned it as the Sector diagram, with area proportional to concentration.
steps.quote: We redesigned the diagram by using an arc starting from the diagram centre

steps.action: They introduce scaling factors for minor ions: 1/average concentration of the dataset, so the average plots at 1 meq/l, based on a reference set of over 6000 analyses; or 1/policy norm for all ions, which gives an 'alarm function'.
steps.quote: we introduced a scaling factor for each of the minor ions, consisting of Fe, SO4 and the nutrients

steps.action: They choose demonstration datasets at regional, national, continental and temporal scales, on the basis of database access and prior peer-reviewed description.
steps.quote: We evaluated our approach for both spatial and temporal applications to demonstrate their wide applicability, for both groundwater and surface water.

steps.action: They plot cluster-derived groundwater types A-F of the central Netherlands (Schot & van der Wal 1992) as Stiff-A diagrams along a flow-system cross-section.
steps.quote: The new Stiff-A diagram in Fig. 1 graphically presents the main groundwater quality types in the central part of the Netherlands

steps.action: They interpret the diagram shapes as water origins and flow-path processes (recharge pollution, reduction in peat, Rhine infiltration, Holocene transgression water) and as suitability for rich fens.
steps.quote: Hydrogeologically, recharge by precipitation on the sandy ridge in the east is reflected in groundwater type A

steps.action: They plot regionally averaged Dutch shallow groundwater (Griffioen et al. 2013) as Jester diagrams, scaled to averages (Fig. 2a) and to drinking-water norms (Fig. 2b), and find that Fe and NH4 exceed the norms in most areas.
steps.quote: while minor ions have been scaled relative to their average concentration over all areas

steps.action: They relate the national patterns to published geochemical controls and state that the diagrams confirm geochemical control dominates anthropogenic control and reveal issues little known to managers.
steps.quote: The diagrams and their differences also confirm that the geochemical control is stronger than the anthropogenic control

steps.action: They replot selected European aquifer-type compositions from the tables of Wendland et al. (2008) as Stiff-B diagrams.
steps.quote: We therefore selected a number of groundwater composition types and plotted them using our new Stiff-B diagram to enable more rapid visual comparison

steps.action: They compare the plotted compositions with Wendland et al.'s assumption that the same aquifer type gives similar groundwater, and report that it does not hold, notably for redox, alkalinity and nutrients.
steps.quote: contrary to the assumption of Wendland et al. (2008), groundwater composition in aquifers from the same typology may differ considerably between and within different countries

steps.action: They plot Jan-Nov 2004 monitoring samples from the Rietspruit River (Vaal catchment) as Sector diagrams, scaled to averages and to South African guidelines.
steps.quote: Fig. 4a presents changes in surface water quality in the form of Sector diagrams over the period Jan-Nov 2004

steps.action: They compare the samples with the norms and read seasonal dilution, persistent PO4 exceedance and a NO3/NH4 reversal, leaving the cause open.
steps.quote: Fig. 4b makes clear that PO4 concentrations exceed the norm set by water quality guidelines more than threefold in every sample

steps.action: They plot identical samples from the four datasets in all four diagram forms, compare their appearance, and report informally that colleagues' preferences differ.
steps.quote: The figure shows how identical samples lead to visually distinctly different diagrams.

steps.action: They vary the scaling basis: averages versus medians (averages more informative), and a uniform cross-area scaling factor, which they could not find without compromising information value.
steps.quote: We examined both using average and using median values of the 6 selected minor ions as a basis for scaling.

steps.action: Because the uniform scaling attempt failed, they settle on area-specific scaling factors and note the resulting limit on cross-dataset comparability, including for norm-based scaling.
steps.quote: We therefore decided to use area specific scaling factors.

steps.action: They retain four diagram forms and two scaling options as a characterized tool and release the R scripts openly.
steps.quote: We developed water quality diagrams which include all four ecohydrologically relevant nutrient species (NO3, NH4, PO4, K).

tree.answer: No phenomenon; a design gap: classical diagrams lack nutrients
Yes; ion concentrations come directly from existing monitoring databases
Build and demonstrate a visual tool (diagrams plus scaling)
No rival hypotheses; alternative diagram forms and scalings only
Conditions found: existing datasets at four scales chosen by access
Partly: average vs median scaling compared; uniform scaling failed, replaced by area-specific

end.claim: Four adapted Stiff- and Maucha-based diagrams show 10 ions, including all four nutrients and four redox-sensitive species, with minor ions scaled to dataset averages or to policy norms; they work for spatial and temporal data, but cross-site comparison is limited by area-specific scaling.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the minor-ion scaling factor (to dataset averages or policy norms), the added nutrients and Fe would be visually negligible beside the macro-ions, and the diagrams would add no ecohydrological information.

gates.evidence: Demonstration datasets were chosen 'primarily based on access of the authors to suitable databases' (p. 4), not by a hypothesis. The tool faced informal checks: the Jester arrows were judged distorting (p. 3), average and median scaling were compared, and a uniform scaling attempt failed (p. 10). There is no criterion under which the diagrams would be judged to fail. Nothing was fixed before the data.

imports.item: Salinity, acidity and nutrients as ecological steering factors for species selection
Maucha ionic diagram and its Broch & Yake (1969) modification scaling arrow length to concentration
EU and Dutch drinking-water norms (Drinkwaterbesluit 2011) used as scaling factors
South African Water Quality Guidelines (DWAF 1996) and Resource Quality Objectives (DWS 2016) as norms
R scripts for plotting the diagrams

novelty_claims.quote: The adapted diagrams are innovative with respect to adding comprehensive visual information on the four ecohydrologically relevant nutrient species levels
we found no water quality diagrams that encompass all the main eco(hydro)logically relevant nutrients NO3, NH4, PO4, and K
Ammonium and PO4 are not used at all in classical water quality diagrams.
We could not find any published application to the Stiff or Maucha diagrams.
The National example provided new insight in high PO4, NH4 and/or K nutrient concentrations in the coastal regions

limits:
1. Sources. The supplied XML text contains no body paragraphs, so the coding relies on PDF pages. No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence; the received and revised dates (2021-09-16 and 2022-08-25) suggest substantial revision that cannot be traced.
2. Tests. The four applications are demonstrations on existing published datasets, not tests with a failure criterion.
3. Evaluation by users. Diagram preference rests on unquantified feedback from colleagues; there is no user study or readability test.
4. Interpretations. The regional and national interpretations largely restate findings from the cited source studies (inference). They are best read as consistent with, not independent of, those studies.
5. Sub-claims at other statuses. The continental sub-claim that aquifers of the same typology differ in composition contradicts Wendland et al. (2008). It rests on replotting Wendland's own tables, so it is a reinterpretation of their data at best_explanation status. The temporal sub-claim (persistent PO4 exceedance in the Rietspruit) is an observation, with its causes left open.
6. Scaling and comparability. The paper says the 6000-analysis reference dataset served as a scaling basis 'for all examples', yet defines scaling as relative to each visualised dataset's averages. Which basis each figure uses is therefore not fully clear (inference). Area-specific scaling makes minor ions incomparable across datasets, which the authors acknowledge.
7. Data access. The underlying data are 'available on request'; the code is on GitHub.
8. Composition. none_fits: the walk is a stated need, then design of a tool, then demonstrations, with no rivals. capability_first does not fit because the question precedes the capability, and no phenomenon is established.
9. Check not listed. The Fig. 5 intercomparison (same samples, four forms) compares appearances rather than checking a result, so it is not listed as a method check.

disagreements.target: Wendland et al. (2008), European aquifer typology
disagreements.support: Replotted compositions for the same aquifer types differ markedly between and within countries in redox, alkalinity and nutrients (Fig. 3).
disagreements.quote: contrary to the assumption of Wendland et al. (2008), groundwater composition in aquifers from the same typology may differ considerably between and within different countries

disagreements.target: Classical water quality diagrams (Stiff, Piper, Maucha)
disagreements.support: These diagrams show mainly macro-ions and omit N and P, so they cannot evaluate ecologically relevant parameters or norms.
disagreements.quote: This makes the diagrams unsuitable for evaluating primary ecologically relevant parameters and processes

disagreements.support: The Ionic Ratio gives only a coarse three-end-member distinction and no nutrient information.
disagreements.quote: Remarkably, it does not provide any information on nutrients.

disagreements.target: Wassen et al. (1988) adapted Stiff diagram
disagreements.support: Nutrients appear there only as separate lines, so characteristic water-type shapes are hard to see.
disagreements.quote: However, characteristic shapes representative of certain water types are not easily discerned.
